s10.old: - The close-out packet's "part of the modified count is CRLF-only" is FALSE: 0 of 149 (`git diff` normalises before comparing). CORRECTED 2026-09-19 by the EOL census (below): `git status` CAN show a pure-EOL change as ` M` because it flags on on-disk size vs index-recorded size without comparing content; the 0/149 result still stands (LIVE's index sizes equal the working sizes, 0 phantom ` M` measured). All 147 text files are functional (+7,453/-2,281); 2 are tracked binaries.
s10.why: "the EOL census (below)" is ## Line-ending census and the shared patch cutter, which follows ## Reconcile 2026-09-19 in -drift-reconcile-eol as in the note

s10.old: - How to apply: (1) before any whole-file commit from a shared dirty checkout, run a BEHIND-HEAD census: commits staged with `git apply --cached` or from other worktrees put content in HEAD that the working file never received, and such a file shows ` M` exactly like new work; decide direction by CONTENT (parent of the introducing commit vs HEAD vs live vs any pre-image), never by commit date vs mtime (DE-028); result here: 0 behind, 0 diverged, 20 ambiguous deletions in 11 files to read before committing their groups. (2) Take ONE lock-free snapshot (`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git status --porcelain=v1 -z`, `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`, `diff --cached --name-status -z`; 50 s total here) and have every agent consume it; forbid agents `status`, walks, and anything under `fec/`. (3) `git grep <pattern> main -- fec audits` exceeds the 2-minute tool timeout because of `audits/legfix5`; scope the pathspec. (4) GateGuard demands its four facts for every new file, scratchpad included, and its two facts before the first Bash call - state them and retry the identical call. (5) Opus architect agents with a full up-front brief, explicit forbidden-verb lists and mandatory positive/negative controls returned censuses that survived spot checks; the one weak signal (mtime vs commit date on `audit_full.py`) was caught by the next agent's content test.
s10.why: "the next agent's content test" is time

s10.old: - How to apply: (1) a HEAD-only finding is provisional until the live file is read; run the batched drift census first (three git calls: `ls-tree -r HEAD`, `ls-files`, `hash-object --stdin-paths`; never per-file git on the OneDrive tree). (2) HEAD-based patches must be `git apply --check`ed against a scratch copy of the live file; expect failures in `run_tests.py`, `verify_collector_roster_updates.py`, the staffer surfaces. (3) The highest-value action Paul can take is a reviewed commit pass of the live tree (weights ruling first, see `code-review-five-lanes-2026-09-13` S-5). Related: `live-tree-branch-state-2026-07-14`, `scout-census-traps-2026-09-13`.

- KERNEL in LIVE at `423820d76`: 243 passed / 4 FAILED, 31.9 min; `test_live_patch` green in the runner. Reds: the two baseline reds the laundry-list landing already carried (`test_bill_collision_guards` - missing `backups\bill_directions.PRE-LEGFIX3.csv`; `test_make_staffer_network_html` - unrecognised verdict); `test_staffer_network_section`, red ONLY because its producer child (`build_staffer_network_section.py --root %TEMP%\...\v6-groups-real-role`) sat 14 min with no CPU and no I/O - the test's `subprocess.run` has NO timeout, so one hung child stalls the whole kernel silently (its log is block-buffered and shows nothing) - the assistant killed that one child; and `test_press_baseline_fold` (errors=1 in-kernel, 21/21 OK alone minutes later = flake under load). Lesson: when the kernel log stops growing, list the python process tree with CPU + Win32_Process I/O counters; a leaf with frozen counters is hung, not slow. A token-free local watchdog (kill idle LEAF descendants of the kernel pid after 240 s, log every kill) kept the run bounded; it made 0 kills.

- LAUNCHERS FIXED on Paul's "add the timeouts to run_pipeline and run_tests too" + "land it when the architect is done": `624e593eb` LANDED in LIVE main (mirror current) - `fec/bounded_subprocess.py` = THE shared bounded launcher (`run_bounded(argv, timeout, env, cwd)`: Popen + real temp files + `wait(timeout)` + process-TREE kill via bounded `taskkill /F /T`; any other exception during the wait also kills the tree before propagating, because unwinding releases `.pipeline_run.lock`); constants, NO env dial: chain step 10800 s (2.6x the slowest step on record, 4,148.7 s over 677 step-runs), kernel suite 1800 s; a timeout returns 124 + a note (pid, args) in stderr / step line / Glass Box summary; 124 != tolerated 2, so a timed-out step HALTS the chain even in TOLERANT_STEPS. `test_bounded_subprocess` 19/19. KERNEL in LIVE through it: 246 passed / 2 FAILED in 7.6 min = exactly the two baseline reds. NOT run: the real chain. NOT changed (flagged to Paul): `fec/weekly_refresh.py` own launcher (`:279 communicate(timeout=)`, `:312` unbounded `proc.wait()` after kill; whole-chain bound 7200 s at `:464` is below the 261.6 min the chain once took) - later bounded by `62aea2f76` (see the refresh-reliability topic); per-producer atomicity under a kill unaudited. Review lesson: when replacing `subprocess.run`, keep its `except: kill(); raise` - an architect dropped it and only the inline read caught it. Size a timeout from the Glass Box `pipeline.step` history (`staffer_hang\chain_step_durations.py`), not taste. `Popen.wait(timeout)` on Win 8+ does not count sleep time.

s10.old: `python fec/tools/live_patch.py eol <file>...` prints `size= crlf= lf= lone_cr= class=`; `... drift <a> <b>` exits 0 IDENTICAL_BYTES / 1 EOL_ONLY / 2 CONTENT. In a cutter script load it by file path (import == execution elsewhere in the repo; this module is import-safe): `LiveFile.read(root, rel)`, `insert_after / insert_before / replace / delete` with a one-line or multi-line anchor (matched per line, terminator stripped, exactly one hit or `AnchorError`), `PatchSet().add(f).write(path)` (also writes `<path>.manifest.json`), `prove(patch, {label: (before, after)})`, `check_against(LIVE, patch)`, then `apply_to(LIVE, patch)` or the argv from `apply_argv()`. Keep cut patches OUTSIDE the repo or under a `-text` attribute. Always apply with `-c core.autocrlf=false` (see git behaviour below).

s10.old: - The Project Brain repos had no remote at all; the same day Paul ordered "set up the brain mirror" and they now push themselves from a post-commit hook (see `project-brain-toolkit-2026-08-11`). Then Paul: "add the hook to melange too" (brain D-059): `<live>\.git\hooks\post-commit` and an identical `post-merge` push the branch just committed or merged (ONE branch, never forced, synchronous - measured 0.2-1.2 s; tags not pushed). The hooks dir is shared by all 16 linked worktrees, `C:\Users\pgoff\Mentat` included. A failed push exits 0, appends to `.git\mirror-push-failures.log` and emits one FAIL Glass Box event (source `melange-mirror-hook`) - check that log at close-out; a rewritten (non-fast-forward) branch is never forced, so it stays stale on the mirror until someone decides. Proven by a real empty commit `b99ba565d` on the session branch. Hooks are unversioned: re-create after a re-clone. `git update-ref` / `branch -f` moves fire no hook.

- How to apply: push mirror main at every merge gate (it is not automatic); a future cloud remote (GitHub) is IMPOSSIBLE without history surgery - tracked blobs up to 2.6 GB (`audits/legfix5` packets) vs the 100 MB limit - so never suggest a plain `git push` to GitHub as a quick option. `gh` CLI is not installed. Mirror path is on the same physical C: drive as the working repo (no protection on its own; Carbonite carries it, see Workstation disk and backup). Links: `universal-lane-laws-2026-08-09`, `live-tree-branch-state-2026-07-14`.
s10.why: "see Workstation disk and backup" is the title of another note, topics/2026-08-incident-workstation-disk-and-backup

Note `git worktree remove` can fail Permission-denied where python `shutil.rmtree` succeeds - restore -> rmtree -> prune is the reliable discard sequence. ALSO: the live tree carries another lane's UNCOMMITTED `.claude/commands/metaloop.md` amendment (glasseye mechanised 2026-08-14: hook mirror measured dead, derived-fanout override; runtime half already deployed - terminal receipts now carry a `fanout` block). Leave it to its lane; never clobber or commit it.

s10.old: - Why this bites: the skills treat the live tree as "canonical" and assume live == main. But `paths.py` ROOT resolves to this tree for DATA regardless of which worktree's CODE you run (qualified by the 2026-07-15 `MONEYBALL_ROOT` correction above). (1) `audit_full.py` reads live SOURCE files via `B = ROOT` (e.g. `open(B+r'\fec\templates\make_member_desk_00.tpl')`), so it audits the live tree's checked-out branch, not yours - it can report FAILURES that belong to another branch's uncommitted state (2026-07-14: the assistant's worktree audit reported 3 desk-psychometric FAILs - checks 497/507/513 - because the live codex template lacked the `5/5 evidence` strings its own audit expects; the assistant's branch template satisfied all 3; zero to do with the change). (2) Running the chain from your worktree writes the SHARED live artifacts, so you can transiently overwrite another session's display artifacts.
